openUiAnatomy: no published Open UI accordion anatomy — union of shadcn's canonical 'accordion' (a thin data-slot wrapper around the external, unvendored `radix-ui` package's Accordion primitive — the SAME external-package boundary DROPDOWN-MENU-MATRIX.md and TOAST-MATRIX.md already recorded for their own shadcn columns) and Salt's real, live `Accordion`/`AccordionGroup`/`AccordionHeader`/`AccordionPanel` family. M3 is a genuine FIRST for this pipeline: not a token-poor edition gap (alert/progress/spinner's shape) and not a tokens-only component (toast/snackbar's shape) but a TOTAL, CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no accordion, expansion-panel, or disclosure component or token family exists anywhere in `3-source/material-web`, verified by both a name grep across the whole clone AND a `find`-based top-level directory listing (the clone's own component folders: button, checkbox, chips, dialog, divider, fab, field, iconbutton, list, menu, progress, radio, select, slider, switch, tabs, textfield — no accordion-shaped entry among them). See DROPDOWN-MENU-MATRIX.md finding 7 / this doc's own Finding 1 for why that forces every row's policy to 'switchable' rather than 'locked' (a locked row that is off for one column fails gen-from-template.py, and every row here is off for M3).

behavior.pattern: One or more collapsible ITEMs, each a header/trigger button paired with a content panel. Click, Enter, or Space on a trigger toggles its own panel. A GROUP of items may enforce single-open-at-a-time exclusivity (shadcn's `type="single"`) or allow several open simultaneously (`type="multiple"`) — Salt has NO group-level exclusivity mechanism at all: each `Accordion` instance owns its own independent boolean state, and `AccordionGroup` is purely a presentational border wrapper (see Finding 2). Keyboard roving-focus between triggers (ArrowUp/Down, Home/End) is part of the documented Radix/APG accordion pattern shadcn inherits but is CONFIRMED ABSENT from Salt's own source (no keydown handler anywhere in `packages/core/src/accordion/`, see Finding 3).
behavior.chassis: skeleton/accordion.tsx — written from the template's part union; inherits from no design system. Content stays PERMANENTLY MOUNTED in the DOM (native `hidden` + `aria-hidden` + a CSS grid-template-rows transition, Salt's own real technique — see Finding 4) rather than the mount/unmount-on-animation-end technique Radix's own `Presence` utility uses internally for shadcn (external, unvendored, not independently reproducible at that mechanism level) — a declared, reasonable simplification, not a silent one, matching the shape of DROPDOWN-MENU-MATRIX.md's one-level-submenu simplification.
